result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Read-only security specialist scanned first-party application, configuration, Bicep, deployment scripts and hooks.
Code-derived SQL provisioning password affects CWE-259 and CWE-798; failed-login security logging pattern affects CWE-778. No secret values reproduced.
Static review only; tests, generated code, vendored libraries and agent definitions excluded. Deployed credentials, permissions and external monitoring not verified.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: SQL provisioning derives the administrator password from a source-defined literal template and deterministic uniqueString(resource-group ID, environment name). The resulting credential is reproducible from deployment metadata and source rather than secret random input; the credential value is intentionally not reproduced.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: LoginModel.OnPostAsync returns failed authentication results without recording an application security event; the model has no logger or audit integration. Default application configuration suppresses ASP.NET Core informational messages. This is a confirmed logging weakness, not an independently exploitable vulnerability; external monitoring and deployed logging overrides were not verified.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: SQL administrator provisioning consumes a credential constructed from a code-defined literal template and deterministic deployment identifiers. A reader of the source with resource-group and environment metadata can reconstruct it. Credential values are withheld.
